**Evidence**

- **Sources present and used correctly.** Two primary City of Surrey URLs (the July 22 Newton parks announcement and the capital-projects page) are cited (lines 66-69) and match the qualified-candidates research record (`2026-07-23-0630-qualified-candidates.json:79-86`, `confidence: "verified-primary-source"`). Every substantive claim is attributed ("Surrey says," "the city says," "Surrey's capital-projects page also lists").

- **Factual/internal consistency holds.** Funding math is consistent: $16.5M (Surrey) + $11M (federal) = the $27.5M headline figure (lines 36, 38). Timing is consistent across title, subtitle, description, and body ("work begins this summer, starting with the covered sport court at Unwin Park," line 62). The "covered sport court" (line 52) vs. "open-air building designed for multiple sports" (line 58) are compatible (roofed but open-sided).

- **No unsupported claims.** Specific amenities (turf field, four lighted tennis courts, field house, pickleball/tennis/basketball courts, spray-park upgrade, access improvements) are all framed as what Surrey "says" is planned, not as guaranteed completed facts. The piece explicitly caveats the limit of the evidence: "it does not provide a complete amenity-by-amenity construction calendar" (line 64) and advises readers to check official updates before planning (line 62-64).

- **Title/subtitle/description/meta fit.** Title is attributed and non-overpromising; subtitle and description accurately summarize the two-park scope, funding, and start timing without exceeding the body.

- **Structure & reader usefulness.** Logical flow (announcement → each park → what to watch), scannable bulleted amenity list, and a concrete practical takeaway (watch Surrey's project updates before planning). Matches the bulletin storyType and lengthRationale.

- **Frontmatter/image integrity.** All required fields present and internally consistent (slug matches filename, locality/tags/category aligned, `status: release-candidate`, approval flags all false/consistent). Image path, descriptive alt text, and AI-generation attribution are all present (lines 6-8).

- **Reputational/legal risk.** Low — no private parties, no enforcement/allegation content, purely a positive municipal capital-project notice fully attributed to official sources. Brand-safety "standard" is appropriate.
